## Document File Preview — Office (OP)

The Office families' renderer: `.docx`, `.pptx`, `.xlsx`.

### Why it renders structure, not the document

The browser **cannot display an Office file natively** — unlike the PDF viewer's native `<object>`. So this renders the structure the extractor read out of the package:

| Kind | What is drawn |
|---|---|
| document | the text flow |
| deck | the slide outline |
| workbook | the sheet grid |

### One component, three families

They share a stage, a fitted placeholder, and the same provenance — *"structured information derived from the source"* — so this is one component that branches on the file's `previewKind` for the domain-specific body. Three near-identical components would have tripled the surface for one differing block.

### The fitted poster is deliberately absent

A first-page/first-slide poster is **not drawn here**. It needs the derived-artifact contract to rasterize and store a real rendition.

Once that lands and populates `thumbnailUrl`, the preview stage prefers the real poster over the typed placeholder **automatically, with no change to this component**. That is why the placeholder is typed rather than generic — it is holding a shape the real artifact will fill.


Projected into the four format shells by `FilePreviewStage`, which owns the loading, failure and staleness panes.
